title: Summis Desiderantes Affectibus: Papal Bull Authorizes Kramer's Witch-Hunt
description: Pope Innocent VIII issued the papal bull Summis desiderantes affectibus on December 5, 1484, authorizing Heinrich Kramer (Institoris) and Jacob Sprenger to pursue witchcraft prosecutions in Germany after Kramer had been blocked by local ecclesiastical authorities. The bull declared that many persons in Germany had abandoned themselves to demons, inflicting harm on men, women, animals, and crops, and commanded ecclesiastical and civil authorities to cooperate with the inquisitors. Kramer subsequently included the text of the bull as a preface to the Malleus Maleficarum (1487), giving the impression that the book itself had papal endorsement — a misleading claim that nonetheless enhanced the text's authority enormously.
historiographical_note: Christopher Mackay's critical edition and translation of the Malleus Maleficarum (2006) carefully disentangles the relationship between Summis desiderantes and Kramer's text, showing that the bull did not endorse the Malleus itself. Historians have debated whether the bull represented a genuine papal initiative or was largely the result of Kramer lobbying Rome after local opposition; the balance of evidence suggests the latter.
source_method: Papal registers; Innocent VIII, Summis desiderantes (1484); Mackay critical edition (2006)
